newsitem.title: USA: Coltec to close Roscoe, Ill., plant.
newsitem.headline: Coltec to close Roscoe, Ill., plant.

text.p: Coltec Industries said on Wednesday it would shut its facility in Roscoe, Illinois, and move businesses operating there to Kentucky and Connecticut.
This transfer, scheduled to be completed in May, was expected to affect 55 Coltec employees, the company said.
The company said it would move its FMD ignition systems business from its Roscoe plant to its Holley Performance Products plant in Kentucky.
The Delavan level control measuring systems operations would be moved from Roscoe to the company's Lewis Engineering unit in Connecticut.
A Coltec spokesman said most of the 55 Roscoe employees would lose their jobs, but the company would not take a charge.

"Both the ignition systems and level control measurement businesses will have far greater growth prospects by becoming part of larger divisions that have the resources to help them develop, manufacture and market new products," said chairman John Guffey, Jr.

FMD ignition systems are used primarily in engines that transmit natural gas through pipelines and Delavan level control systems measure the levels of liquids and solids across a spectrum of industries, including petroleum, chemicals, utilities, food and mining.
